question: Do pretrained language models execute a reusable arithmetic algorithm, retrieve memorized equations, or combine many input-conditioned neural heuristics to answer basic single-token arithmetic prompts?

key_findings.claim: The localized Llama3-8B arithmetic circuit routes the two operands and operator to the final position, where middle- and late-layer MLPs promote answer tokens.
key_findings.evidence: Activation patching finds a small operator-dependent set of attention heads and broad MLP involvement. Three general heads copy operand 1, the operator, and operand 2 to the final position. A linear probe recovers the answer only at that position from roughly layer 16 onward. With all MLPs, 6 heads suffice for addition, subtraction, and division at 0.97, 0.98, and 0.96 faithfulness, while multiplication uses 20 heads at 0.90.

key_findings.claim: A relatively sparse subset of MLP neurons is sufficient under the paper's circuit-faithfulness intervention, but the resulting mechanism still contains thousands of neurons per operator.
key_findings.evidence: The authors retain the top 200 neurons in each of 16 middle-to-late layers—about 1.5% per layer and 3,200 neurons per operator—and report high faithfulness after mean-ablating lower-effect neurons and non-circuit components. Operator-specific sets have average intersection-over-union 54%, so about 45% of important neurons are unique to an operator.

anchors.section: 3.1 Decomposing Circuit MLPs to Individual Neurons

key_findings.claim: The neuron taxonomy supports a logit-voting account: distinct neurons respond to operand/result ranges, residues, digit patterns, equal operands, or small answer sets and jointly promote the correct token.
key_findings.evidence: For each high-effect neuron, the method combines its activation grid over operand pairs with Logit-Lens projections of its output vector, then compares its top-k prompts with prompts generated by a candidate rule. At a 0.6 intersection threshold, 91% of the 3,200 selected neurons per operator match at least one manually defined heuristic. Direct heuristics promote result tokens; indirect heuristics encode operand features for later processing.

anchors.section: 3.2 MLP Neurons Act as Memorized Heuristics

key_findings.claim: Targeted knockouts establish that classified neurons causally contribute to associated prompts, but not that the hand-built taxonomy is a complete or unique decomposition.
key_findings.evidence: Zeroing all neurons assigned to one heuristic lowers accuracy on associated prompts by 29 percentage points from a 95% mean, more than on non-associated prompts. Prompt-specific removal of neurons from all applicable heuristic classes harms accuracy more than removing equally many neurons from unassociated classes across Llama3-8B/70B, Pythia-6.9B, and GPT-J. However, categories overlap, 9% of selected neurons remain unclassified, the 0.6 threshold lacks labeled ground truth, and the paper does not compare alternative learned taxonomies or magnitude-matched feature interventions.

anchors.section: 4.2 Heuristic Types Are Combined to Answer Arithmetic Prompts

key_findings.claim: The behavioral scope is basic single-token arithmetic, so the evidence does not justify a general claim about how LLMs solve multi-digit mathematics or chain-of-thought problems.
key_findings.evidence: Prompts contain exactly four tokens and operands are restricted to 0 through 300; prompts with negative or split-token results are removed. Llama3-8B averages 0.95 accuracy, but Llama3-70B averages 0.88, Pythia-6.9B 0.43, and GPT-J 0.37. Half of legal integer-division prompts for the smaller models output zero, inflating their division accuracy. Circuit discovery and most probes further condition on prompts the model already answers correctly.

anchors.section: H Model Accuracies on Arithmetic Prompts

key_findings.claim: The failure analysis favors insufficient correct-logit contribution over too few associated heuristic neurons, but it is a small descriptive audit rather than a predictive failure model.
key_findings.evidence: Among 50 correct and 50 incorrect Llama3-8B prompts, incorrect cases have at least as many associated heuristic neurons; correct cases instead have a slightly higher summed activation-times-output-logit contribution to the target. No held-out classifier, calibration curve, competing wrong-token analysis, or intervention that repairs predicted failures is reported.

anchors.section: 4.3 Failure Modes of the Bag of Heuristics

key_findings.claim: Pythia checkpoint analysis shows continuity of final heuristic neurons after arithmetic performance has emerged, not the mechanism from the onset of pretraining.
key_findings.evidence: The trajectory starts at step 23K because it is the earliest checkpoint with good arithmetic accuracy, then samples every 10K steps to 143K. Final-checkpoint heuristic neurons appear progressively; neurons shared with the final checkpoint account for 79% of total heuristic contribution on average, and prompt-targeted knockout remains damaging. Earlier checkpoints are not analyzed, and identifying a feature by the same neuron index assumes functional identity despite representational drift.

anchors.section: 5 Tracking Heuristics Development Across Training Steps

method.core_idea: Localize arithmetic behavior causally, decompose the influential MLPs into individual neurons, assign human-readable numerical rules to their activation-and-output patterns, and test whether ablating the rules relevant to a prompt destroys its answer.
method.mechanism: Activation patching selects heads and MLPs; mean-ablation estimates circuit faithfulness; per-neuron patching ranks MLP units; activation grids and Logit Lens expose input conditions and promoted outputs; a rule-matching algorithm labels high-effect neurons; heuristic- and prompt-conditioned knockouts test necessity; Pythia checkpoints track persistence during training.
assumptions: Mean-ablating all non-circuit components preserves the relevant computation without introducing off-distribution artifacts.
A neuron is an appropriate primitive despite polysemanticity and distributed features.
Human-specified range, modulo, digit-pattern, equality, and multi-result rules span the important arithmetic abstractions.
A 0.6 top-prompt overlap threshold separates genuine rule implementation from incidental correlation.
Single-token arithmetic over operands at most 300 is representative of broader arithmetic reasoning.
A neuron at the same parameter index across checkpoints retains a comparable feature.

techniques.role: Localizes operand/operator transport and answer-promoting model components.
Measures normalized correct-token logit retained by a proposed circuit.
Locates when and where the target answer becomes linearly decodable.
Ranks individual MLP units within arithmetic-relevant layers.
Labels units by overlap between effective logit grids and parameterized numerical rules.
Tests the causal relevance of the union of heuristics applicable to a prompt.
Follows final-checkpoint heuristic neurons through Pythia training.

evaluations.setting: Llama3-8B single-token addition, subtraction, multiplication, and integer division
evaluations.result: 0.97, 0.98, 0.90, and 0.96 with 6, 6, 20, and 6 heads plus MLPs
evaluations.baseline: Full model and fully mean-ablated model

evaluations.result: 91% of selected neurons per operator match at least one defined heuristic at threshold 0.6
evaluations.baseline: Manual inspection of unclassified high-effect neurons

evaluations.setting: 100 associated and 100 non-associated correct prompts per heuristic

evaluations.setting: Prompt-guided neuron ablation in Llama3-8B/70B, Pythia-6.9B, and GPT-J
evaluations.result: Associated-heuristic neurons cause consistently larger accuracy drops than equally sized unassociated-neuron sets.

evaluations.metric: heuristic persistence, circuit contribution, and knockout accuracy
evaluations.result: Final heuristics emerge gradually; shared neurons explain 79% of heuristic contribution on average; targeted 25-neuron-per-layer ablation drives accuracy near zero.
evaluations.baseline: All checkpoint-local heuristic neurons and random important-neuron ablation

evaluations.setting: All legal single-token prompts with operands in 0-300

limitations: The taxonomy is manually designed and its matching threshold is manually selected without neuron-level ground truth.
Neurons can match several rules, remain unclassified, or encode superposed non-arithmetic functions, making the decomposition non-unique.
Most analyses select correctly answered prompts, which can obscure mechanisms responsible for errors and overstate coverage of overall behavior.
Inputs and answers must each be single tokens and operands stop at 300; multi-token carrying, long multiplication, expressions, word problems, and chain-of-thought are excluded.
Integer-division answer imbalance inflates apparent accuracy, especially for Pythia and GPT-J.
Zeroing heuristic neurons may be more distribution-shifting than mean, resampling, or subspace interventions and is not activation-magnitude matched.
Circuit faithfulness is a normalized correct-logit proxy rather than exact distributional or behavioral equivalence.
Training analysis begins only after useful arithmetic performance and covers one model family.
The four models share broad decoder-only and tokenizer conventions; digit-level tokenization is explicitly untested.
failure_modes: A prompt can activate many nominally relevant neurons yet receive too little combined target-logit support.
Low-recall heuristics fail to activate for all inputs satisfying their human-assigned rule.
A neuron's output can also promote a competing answer, which the target-only contribution score ignores.
Manual range or regex discretization can assign a nearby approximate rule rather than the feature actually represented.
Polysemantic neuron ablation can harm arithmetic indirectly by removing other computation.
Tokenization changes can replace one-token lookup-like geometry with digit-wise algorithms.
Heuristic voting can interpolate within the sampled number range while failing systematic length extrapolation.
reusable_insights: Combine localization with prompt-specific causal interventions; high activation or a compelling visualization alone is insufficient.
Measure mechanism coverage on both correct and incorrect examples and predict failures prospectively.
Test taxonomies against automatically discovered rules, held-out operand regions, counterfactual formats, and matched-size random feature sets.
Report circuit size in absolute units as well as per-layer percentage.
Cross tokenizers and digit lengths before generalizing a numerical mechanism to arithmetic reasoning broadly.
Treat representation-level algorithms and neuron-level heuristics as potentially compatible levels of description, then intervene to distinguish them.
open_questions: Can an automatic rule learner recover the same neurons and discover the unexplained 9% without a human-authored taxonomy?
Are the helix/Clock representation and bag-of-heuristics neurons complementary layers of one computation or competing explanations?
Do the same causal features support symbolic equations, word problems, code, and multi-step chain-of-thought?
What mechanism emerges with digit-level tokenization and length-extrapolating arithmetic curricula?
Can a target-logit contribution model predict and repair unseen failures, including which wrong answer wins?
Do feature-level or subspace interventions reproduce neuron knockout results while controlling polysemantic collateral damage?
What happens before Pythia step 23K, and can feature alignment track changing representations without assuming neuron-index identity?
Does the heuristic repertoire grow with model and data scale, or converge toward a more compact algorithm?

competitive_landscape.title: A Mechanistic Interpretation of Arithmetic Reasoning in Language Models using Causal Mediation Analysis
competitive_landscape.difference: Stolfo et al. establish the early-attention transport and later-MLP result-processing architecture through causal mediation across arithmetic questions. The reviewed paper reproduces and narrows that circuit, then contributes a neuron-level rule taxonomy and prompt-conditioned causal knockout intended to explain what the MLPs compute.

competitive_landscape.title: Language Models Use Trigonometry to Do Addition
competitive_landscape.difference: Kantamneni and Tegmark find a generalized helical number representation and propose a causal Clock algorithm for addition across three mid-sized LLMs, modeling heads, MLP outputs, and neuron preactivations. This challenges a flat no-algorithm reading, although helix features could be the shared numerical basis from which the reviewed paper's local heuristics read and write; a head-to-head intervention is needed.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: McLeish et al. add digit-position embeddings and train on at most 20-digit inputs yet reach up to 99% accuracy on 100-digit addition, with gains on sorting and multiplication. Their controlled models are not pretrained LLMs, but they show that transformer arithmetic can length-generalize when tokenization and positional structure support an algorithm—the exact regime excluded by the reviewed study.

competitive_landscape.title: Are Arithmetic Heuristic Neurons Form-Invariant? A Mechanistic Analysis of Symbols, Text, and Code in LLMs
competitive_landscape.difference: Naganna et al. identify a compact neuron set shared across symbolic arithmetic, word problems, and Python in three Llama-3 models; targeted necessity/sufficiency tests and cross-format activation transfer recover over 97% of failed addition/subtraction cases. This supports the reviewed paper's heuristic-neuron premise while addressing its format restriction, though it remains within one model family and is under review.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Pretrained LLMs solve basic arithmetic with neither a robust algorithm nor equation memorization, but with an unordered bag of sparse MLP-neuron heuristics that emerges early in training.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper causally localizes an arithmetic circuit, shows high faithfulness with selected neurons, maps most high-effect units to numerical rule families, performs heuristic- and prompt-specific knockouts across four models, studies correct and incorrect prompts, and follows Pythia checkpoints.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest novelty is the prompt-conditioned causal bridge from a human-readable neuron taxonomy to model answers, beyond prior component-level localization. The experiments convincingly show that these neurons matter in the narrow single-token regime. They do not exclude a distributed representation-level algorithm, establish that the chosen taxonomy is unique, or generalize to digit-wise and multi-step arithmetic; the title is therefore memorable but broader than the demonstrated scope.
